options.label: Slim memories to pointers (Recommended)
options.description: Each memory file becomes a short stub: "See notes/<file>.md for the canonical version." Keeps Claude aware the topic exists; the real content lives in notes/. One source of truth.

options.label: Keep both, duplicated
options.description: Memory files stay as-is. Notes are a separate human-facing copy. Risk: they drift apart when you edit one and not the other.

questions.question: Should notes/ be tracked in git?

options.label: Track (current default)
options.description: notes/ will be committed when you commit. Target companies, prep plan, network ideas live in repo history.

options.label: Gitignore notes/

## On the website next step

Since stack isn't decided and nothing is deployed, the cheapest unlock is to invert the order: **write one project page first, pick the stack second.** Reasons:

- The stack matters less than the *story* — recruiters bounce on weak copy, not on whether you used Astro or Next.
- The shape of the content tells you what stack you need. If the dstrader writeup is plain prose + a few diagrams + an eval table, a static-site generator like Astro is overkill and a single hand-written HTML page works. If you want interactive eval explorers or live demos, Next/SvelteKit earns its keep.
- The flagship page — per [[position-thesis-agent-spec]] — is the dstrader/FamilyFund "agentic research layer over a live trading system" narrative. That's the one a hiring manager actually reads. Write that as a markdown draft first, then decide hosting.

Concrete suggestion for the next session on this: draft the dstrader project page as plain markdown (no framework). Once we see the content, the stack decision becomes a 5-minute choice instead of a multi-hour evaluation.
